title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
task: Learning unified tactile representation across heterogeneous sensors for dexterous manipulation
key_results: LingBot-Touch enables plug-and-play integration across piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors; consistently improves manipulation performance on real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms
comments: Strong practical contribution addressing sensor diversity, though evaluation primarily focuses on task success rather than transfer learning metrics across sensor types.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-sensor tactile representations can transfer between diverse sensor hardware

task: Unified infrastructure and evaluation for generative world models across modalities
key_results: WorldFoundry catalog: 270 models, 74 benchmarks, 62 metrics; enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across video, 3D/4D, embodied, and interactive systems
comments: Excellent infrastructure contribution but lacks concrete performance comparisons; value lies in standardization and reproducibility rather than novel methods.

title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
task: Metacognitive architecture for scientific discovery and ideation
key_results: Sage-Taiyi ranks first on Taiyi-Bench (54.0 vs 47.9 baseline); validated chemistry yields: cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation 0% → 84%, photocatalytic allylic amination 13% → 69%
comments: Impressive empirical validation with real experimental results; metacognition-inspired design is novel but the paper's depth on mechanism remains unclear.

title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
task: Post-training visual agents to align observations and handle tool-returned data in RL/distillation
key_results: Reframe outperforms Mix-RL and vanilla MOPD across 14 image/video benchmarks; GD-GRPO increases observation dependence and tool gain vs outcome-based GRPO
comments: Novel observation-alignment perspective in distillation, though the two-stage approach adds complexity; gains appear incremental on individual benchmarks.

title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
task: Efficient inference engine for decision models in LLM agent systems
key_results: Flide: 9.5× faster than vLLM/SGLang on decision model queries; exact arithmetic with ForkAttention; stays closest to float32 reference in total variation distance
comments: Strong systems contribution with clear speedup; the decoupling of logical and physical execution is elegant, though specialized to decision-tree workloads.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ForkAttention maintains exactness with 9.5× speedup

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
task: Standardized artifact design and agent workflows for reproducible ML experiments
key_results: ReproBridge-Bench: 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments; refined artifacts raise reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6%, reduce API cost by 19.7%, narrow model spread from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points
comments: Pragmatic contribution showing execution knowledge matters for reproducibility; standardized artifacts are impactful but the approach is straightforward engineering.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Preserving execution knowledge improves agent reproduction success

title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
task: Repository-level SWE benchmark for underrepresented programming languages
key_results: 202 high-quality issue-resolution tasks across 13 languages; solver-judge-repairer pipeline improved task quality by correcting invalid tests and descriptions
comments: Addresses a genuine gap in SWE benchmarks, though the relatively small task count per language (≈15 tasks) may limit statistical significance for fine-grained model comparisons.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Solver-judge-repairer pipeline improves benchmark quality by filtering defective tasks

title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
task: Recursive self-improvement for distributed LLM training infrastructure optimization
key_results: InfraRSI: up to 2.75× speedup, lifts MFU from 17.4% to 30.0% across dense and MoE workloads; outperforms existing tuners while transferring experience across GPUs
comments: Sophisticated agentic approach with verification mechanisms and experience distillation; the two-level RSI loop is innovative, though evaluation focuses on speedup without discussing potential hidden costs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Recursive self-improvement can optimize tightly coupled training infrastructure

task: Evaluating LLM ability to judge when simulator errors invalidate systems design recommendations
key_results: Frontier LLMs cannot reliably distinguish valid from invalid simulator-based recommendations; self-correction helps but introduces new errors; even identifying limitations does not ensure correct choice
comments: Important diagnostic showing systems reasoning gaps in LLMs; limited in scope (LLM serving problems) but highlights a critical real-world failure mode.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs can distinguish valid from invalid simulator recommendations

task: Understanding training-inference mismatch tolerance in on-policy distillation
key_results: OPD tolerates substantial quantization mismatch without quality loss up to empirical budget; FP8 recipes preserve quality with 1.93× more KV-cache tokens than BF16; synchronous BF16 training reaches same quality 1.62× slower

hypotheses.hypothesis: OPD tolerates substantial quantization without quality loss

title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
task: Adapting RL objectives for few-step diffusion models
key_results: Few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD, ReFL in single modular codebase; reward-gradient methods most effective when reward is differentiable; extra inference steps show no systematic aggregate benefit
comments: Principled adaptation framework with thorough ablations; however, practical speedup gains over many-step models remain unclear from abstract.

task: Multi-agent task refinement with iterative optimization for retrieval-augmented generation
key_results: TRIO outperforms state-of-the-art across multiple benchmark datasets; effective at improving answer quality through query extension, unanimity voting, and curriculum-learned answer generation
comments: Solid multi-agent refinement approach with clear reward alignment; evaluation spans multiple benchmarks but lacks explicit quantitative comparisons to baselines.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aligning individual agent objectives improves RAG performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM agents can optimize O2O commerce operations over 180 days

task: Improving spatial attention head specialization in Vision Transformers via focusing loss
key_results: Focusing loss increases spatial selectivity and diversity of attention heads; improves performance on dense prediction tasks (zero-shot segmentation) without annotations; substantially increases interpretability

task: Lightweight high-fidelity voxel generation via joint hierarchical flow matching
key_results: JoVox: 8× higher training throughput, 1/15 FLOPs vs TRELLIS.2, trains on 4 vs 32 GPUs; 11% lower Chamfer distance; outperforms on unconditional and image-conditioned generation

key_results: Lowers validation loss in 11/12 comparisons and raises downstream task accuracy in 10/12 comparisons; cost is one extra embedding table
